name: Morning Brew

sources.title: Morning Brew FAQ — advertising goes through the partnership request form; brand partnerships team responds 'if it seems like a good fit' (content read via search result; homepage 403)
Morning Brew Inc contact — hello@morningbrew.com for general inquiries; advertising form matches you with an account manager (content read via search result)

conditions: No listing/submission product at all — Morning Brew is a newsletter media company; the only documented public routes are the contact form (hello@morningbrew.com) and paid advertising via the partnership form
requirements: Earned coverage route: pitch hello@morningbrew.com or the contact form — the Brew covers business/tech news it finds interesting, there is no tips desk documented
Paid route: partnership request form → brand partnerships team
Newsletter-native voice — sponsored content is produced in Morning Brew's style
Audience is business-news readers, not product hunters
preparation: A genuinely newsworthy business story (funding, trend, quirky data) for the earned route
A budget and brand brief for the advertising route
workflow: Earned: send a concise pitch to hello@morningbrew.com or via morningbrewinc.com/contact
Paid: fill the partnership request form; an account manager responds if it's a fit
There is no self-serve listing — everything is editorial or sales-mediated
watchFor: morningbrew.com blocked automated fetch (403) — details verified via the FAQ and Morning Brew Inc. pages
The old '60 Second Startup' pitch-to-Alex-Lieberman segment is historical — don't rely on it
Massive audience — a cold pitch needs a real story, not a launch announcement
countsAsLive: A Morning Brew story or sponsored segment mentioning the product runs in the newsletter/site
unknowns: Whether the newsroom accepts unsolicited pitches at a separate editorial address
